They fill balast tanks with water until the overall sub has the same density as sea water at a particular depth. This makes the sub 'neutrally boyant' at that depth--neither sinking lower nor floating higher. If you could instantly skim an inch of water off the top of the ocean, the sub would sink an inch because it'd be slightly more dense than the reduced amount of water above it. A similar phenomena occurs as the sub travels laterally across the face of the Earth with the sub always remaining at the equilibrium depth instead of approaching the surface. This happens so incrementally/continuously that it's basically imperceptible.
